stem:
Kavya looks at the diagram of a rectangle $10\,\mathrm{cm}$ by $6\,\mathrm{cm}$ with a rectangular hole $4\,\mathrm{cm}$ by $3\,\mathrm{cm}$ cut from its interior. The hole does not meet the outer edge.

Which claim correctly finds the remaining area?

options.text: Call the answer the outer length $10\,\mathrm{cm}$ alone.
Add the outer rectangle area to the hole area.
Subtract the hole area from the outer rectangle area: $10\times 6 - 4\times 3$.
Use only the printed $4\times 3$ label as the remaining area.

teacher.key_rationale: Remaining area is outer minus hole: 60−12=48. Naming length alone, adding instead of subtracting, or grabbing the hole label miss the decomposition.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source kite-on-grid as outer 10-by-6 rectangle with inner 4-by-3 rectangular hole.
